strings.ROCKNIXDS Pixel's two palettes, dark or: ROCKNIXDS Pixel's two palettes, dark or light for daylight; or a theme of your own: a .json in banana/themes on the card (banana/themes/README.txt says how).
strings.The language of the Settings screen: Eng: The language of the Settings screen: English, Spanish or German. The other screens follow in a later update.
strings.The panel's backlight. F + volume change: The panel's backlight. F + volume changes it anywhere, in games too.
strings.The speakers or the headphones, whicheve: The speakers or the headphones, whichever is playing. The volume keys change it anywhere.
strings.The menu's clicks, and the cartridge goi: The menu's clicks, and the cartridge going into the console.
strings.An ambient loop under the menu, mixed lo: An ambient loop under the menu, mixed low so the clicks stay clear. Put a bgm.wav (or music/bgm.wav) on the card to hear one. Off stops it at once.
strings.The battery on the top screen: its icon,: The battery on the top screen: its icon, or its icon and how full it is.
strings.How the time on the top screen is writte: How the time on the top screen is written.
strings.The bananas and the cartridge while Bana: The bananas and the cartridge while Banana starts. Off goes straight to the menu once it is ready.
strings.In the menu, after this long with no but: In the menu, after this long with no button pressed. Never while a game is running.
strings.In the menu, the panel goes down to a th: In the menu, the panel goes down to a third after this long with no button pressed, and back at the first press. Never while a game is running.
strings.Softcore: achievements unlock with save: Softcore: achievements unlock with save states, rewind and cheats still there. Hardcore: those are locked for the game, and the unlocks count as hardcore on retroachievements.org. RetroArch's own menu changes the same setting.
strings.On: quitting keeps where you are, and th: On: quitting keeps where you are, and the game goes on from there next time (RetroArch's automatic save state; not in Hardcore). Off: a game starts from its title.
strings.The emulator for GBA games. gpSP: the fa: The emulator for GBA games. gpSP: the fastest. mGBA: the most accurate, and the one RetroAchievements accepts for hardcore.
strings.The emulator for PlayStation games. Swan: The emulator for PlayStation games. SwanStation (DuckStation): hardware rendering and much greater accuracy, heavier. PCSX-ReARMed: lightest, and the one to fall back to when a game is slow.
strings.The emulator for NES games. FCEUmm: the: The emulator for NES games. FCEUmm: the lightest. NEStopia: more accurate, a little heavier.
strings.The emulator for SNES games. Snes9x: fas: The emulator for SNES games. Snes9x: fast, and the usual choice. bsnes: cycle-accurate, much heavier.
strings.The emulator for Game Boy games. Gambatt: The emulator for Game Boy games. Gambatte: fast and accurate. SameBoy: the most accurate, and the one that renders the original LCD best.
strings.The emulator for Game Boy Color games. G: The emulator for Game Boy Color games. Gambatte: fast and accurate. SameBoy: the most accurate.
strings.The emulator for Mega Drive games. PicoD: The emulator for Mega Drive games. PicoDrive: the lightest (32X too). Genesis Plus GX: more accurate for Mega CD.
strings.The emulator for Game Gear games. Genesi: The emulator for Game Gear games. Genesis Plus GX: more accurate. PicoDrive: the lightest (Mega Drive and 32X too).
strings.The emulator for N64 games. Mupen64Plus-: The emulator for N64 games. Mupen64Plus-Next: the usual choice, with its own GLideN64. ParaLLEl N64: the alternative.
strings.The networks around: A on one joins it,: The networks around: A on one joins it, with a password typed on the keyboard here (or by touch). An old WEP network takes its key the same way; a company (802.1X) network still needs banana/wifi.conf by hand.
strings.The clock's time zone, summer time inclu: The clock's time zone, summer time included, for the menu and the games. The time itself comes from Wi-Fi or the handheld's own clock.
strings.A new version of Banana, written to the: A new version of Banana, written to the other slot and run from the next restart; this one stays as it is until then. Over Wi-Fi, "Check for updates" downloads the newest release from GitHub; a package on the card in banana/updates (File sharing can copy one) works too.
strings.Settings, accounts, the saves/states tre: Settings, accounts, the saves/states trees and RetroArch's controller remaps in one file in banana/backups on the card (File sharing can copy it off). Games and box art stay out of it. Press A twice.
strings.Unpacks the newest backup over the card': Unpacks the newest backup over the card's settings, saves and states, then restarts the menu so they are read. Press A twice.
strings.Covers, title screens, genres and years: Covers, title screens, genres and years for your games, from libretro's free collections (no account, Wi-Fi needed). It keeps going in the background; games that already have art are skipped, so running it again only fetches what is new. Starts only on the charger (or the USB cable), so a long scrape cannot flatten the battery.
strings.libretro: libretro's collections. libret: libretro: libretro's collections. libretro + Twilight: TwilightBoxart (boxart.kirovair.com) for the covers libretro has none of. Twilight first: TwilightBoxart's covers where it has them. TwilightBoxart is asked one game a second.
strings.Restarts into the other slot: the versio: Restarts into the other slot: the version that ran before the last update. Press A twice.
strings.The card's games and saves as a USB disk: The card's games and saves as a USB disk on the computer over the cable. Read-only copies off the card; Read-write (transfer mode) stops the menu and hands the card over until you eject it.
strings.Games on the card in the second slot (it: Games on the card in the second slot (its roms folder, with the same system folders as this card) show up in the library with the others while it's in. exFAT or FAT32.
strings.The steps from the first boot again: Wi-: The steps from the first boot again: Wi-Fi, the time zone and the RetroAchievements account.
strings.Puts the menu, display, sound, power and: Puts the menu, display, sound, power and network settings back to their defaults (banana/settings.conf and bananad's sleep rows; your games and card are untouched). Press A twice.
strings.Puts the emulator choices back to their: Puts the emulator choices back to their defaults: the core.<system> picks. Your menu and card settings stay. Press A twice.
